name: Octa
description: Octa (formerly OctaFX) is a multi-entity CFD broker founded in 2011, offering forex and CFD trading on approximately 300 instruments via MT4, MT5, and its proprietary OctaTrader platform. Regulated by CySEC in Cyprus and FSCA in South Africa, with an offshore MISA-licensed entity in Saint Lucia serving most global retail clients.
pros: Commission-free trading across all account types
Low minimum deposit of $25 makes it accessible
Spreads from 0.6 pips on EUR/USD are genuinely competitive for a zero-commission model
Proprietary OctaTrader platform is well-designed for beginners
Islamic (swap-free) accounts available at no extra cost
No deposit or withdrawal fees charged by the broker
cons: CySEC majority shareholder stripped of voting rights following India fraud probe in 2025
ED India investigation: Rs 800 crore money laundering case with chargesheet filed against founder
Most global clients routed to offshore MISA entity in Saint Lucia with zero investor protection
Warned by Malaysia SC, BNM, CNMV, and Indian regulators for unlicensed activities
Limited instrument range (approximately 300) compared to multi-asset competitors
Documented withdrawal complaints in 2026 where funds marked completed never reached bank accounts
Mauritius and Comoros entities split off to form Elev8 in February 2026 creating entity confusion
warning_note: Octa's ultimate beneficial owner Pavel Prozorov has been named as the mastermind in an Indian Enforcement Directorate Rs 800 crore money laundering case (chargesheet filed December 2024). CySEC subsequently stripped his voting rights and barred him from management at Octa Markets Cyprus Ltd in September 2025. The FCA has issued warnings against clone entities using the Octa/OctaFX name. Multiple regulators (Malaysia SC, BNM, CNMV, India ED) have issued warnings or taken enforcement action against the brand for unlicensed activities. Documented 2026 withdrawal complaints exist where transactions marked completed did not reach client bank accounts.

long_review.hot_take: Octa built a genuinely good beginner platform and competitive spread structure — then allowed its founder to allegedly funnel Rs 800 crore through mule accounts in India while the CySEC entity looked the other way. The trading conditions are real. The regulatory crisis is also real. You are effectively betting that the product survives its leadership scandal, and that your offshore-entity funds remain accessible if enforcement actions escalate. That is not a bet most traders should take with money they cannot afford to lose.

sections.heading: Is Octa Worth Your Money in 2026?
sections.body:
Competitive spreads, zero commissions, and a $25 minimum deposit built this broker a user base of over 42 million accounts across 180 countries since 2011. The OctaTrader platform is one of the better proprietary offerings aimed at beginners — clean interface, built-in copy trading, and no unnecessary complexity. For pure trading conditions on a micro-budget, the numbers hold up. Spreads averaging 0.6 pips EUR/USD with no round-turn commission puts Octa cheaper than most brokers charging $7 per lot on raw accounts.

But the organisation behind the product is in serious trouble. Indian authorities have filed a chargesheet naming Octa's ultimate beneficial owner as the mastermind of an Rs 800 crore money laundering scheme. CySEC responded by stripping his voting rights and barring him from management in September 2025. And the Mauritius and Comoros entities that previously operated under the Octa brand split off entirely in February 2026 to form a new broker called Elev8 — leaving the remaining Octa structure smaller and more exposed.

This is a broker for traders who understand exactly which entity holds their money, keep balances small, and withdraw profits the same week they earn them. It is not a broker for anyone looking for long-term capital safety.

sections.heading: Is Octa Regulated? — Licence Check 2026
sections.body:
Yes — but the picture is more complicated than a single licence number suggests. Octa Markets Cyprus Ltd holds CySEC licence 372/18, which means it operates within EU/EEA regulatory frameworks including MiFID II client protections. That entity covers European residents and provides access to the Investor Compensation Fund (ICF) covering up to EUR 20,000 per client.

The South African entity holds an FSCA licence and serves South African residents under local derivative trading rules. But there is no compensation scheme attached — FSCA requires fund segregation, not insurance.

The majority of global retail clients — anyone in Southeast Asia, Africa outside South Africa, Latin America, or the Middle East — land on a MISA-licensed entity based in Saint Lucia. MISA is a Comoros-origin offshore licence. It carries no compensation scheme, no external dispute resolution body with enforcement power, and no meaningful regulatory oversight by international standards.

The critical development: CySEC stripped the voting rights of Octa's majority shareholder Pavel Prozorov in September 2025, following the Indian Enforcement Directorate naming him as mastermind of an Rs 800 crore fraud. The regulator stated his influence was prejudicial to the sound and prudent management of the firm. This means the CySEC entity technically still operates — but under governance constraints that raise serious questions about its future.

NAFT last reviewed Octa regulation in May 2026.

sections.practical_note: India is a grey zone. Octa historically had massive Indian client presence but the ED probe and raids in 2025 have effectively made it non-operational there. Malaysian regulators (SC and BNM) have warned against OctaFX for operating without a licence — yet the broker still appears to accept Malaysian clients. Verify your entity assignment in the client agreement before depositing.

sections.heading: Octa Spreads, Fees and Accounts — What Do You Actually Pay in 2026?
sections.body:
The maths here is straightforward because Octa runs a single-tier pricing model: zero commission on every account type, with the cost embedded entirely in the spread. On EUR/USD your all-in cost is the spread alone — averaging 0.6 pips on OctaTrader and MT5, which translates to $6.00 per standard lot round-turn. MT4 averages slightly wider at 0.9 pips ($9.00 per lot). That puts Octa cheaper than IC Markets Standard ($8.00) and roughly equal to Exness Standard on the flagship pair.

No inactivity fee. No deposit fee. No withdrawal fee. No swap on Islamic accounts. The fee structure is genuinely clean — which is how Octa attracted 42 million accounts despite offering fewer than 300 instruments.

The catch is leverage. If you are under the CySEC entity you get 1:30 on majors, 1:20 on minors, and 1:10 on commodities — standard EU retail caps. If you are on the offshore MISA entity, you get up to 1:500. That is not a feature — it is how brokers extract maximum risk from under-capitalised accounts. And the offshore entity has no circuit breaker if things go wrong.

table.footnote: All spread figures are broker-stated averages. Independently verified data from public comparison sites reports average EUR/USD between 0.6-0.9 pips as of April 2026.

sections.heading: How Fast Can You Get Your Money Out of Octa?
sections.body:
Deposits are instant via card and e-wallet — that part works. Crypto deposits (Bitcoin, USDT) take up to 3 hours for network confirmation. Bank transfers are the slowest at 1-3 business days.

Withdrawals are where Octa's story gets complicated. The broker states most withdrawals process within 24 hours — and for many traders, particularly on e-wallets and crypto, that claim appears to hold. But publicly reported complaints from Q1 2026 document cases where withdrawals were marked as completed in the client portal while funds never reached the destination bank account. That pattern — status says done, money never arrives — is one of the most dangerous complaint types because it removes your ability to escalate within the broker's own system.

No withdrawal fees are charged by Octa itself (broker-stated). Third-party payment processor fees may still apply depending on your method and region.

table.footnote: Processing times are broker-stated. Independent reports suggest e-wallet withdrawals generally process within hours, but bank transfer and larger crypto withdrawals may experience delays.

sections.heading: Octa Withdrawals in 2026 — The Real Picture
sections.body:
Trustpilot data for Octa is limited — the broker does not appear to have a highly active Trustpilot presence with verifiable volume. Public review platforms show mixed signals: many traders report same-day withdrawals via Skrill and Neteller with no issues. The broker's internal claim of processing most requests within 19 minutes may apply to automated e-wallet payouts.

The complaint pattern that matters in 2026 is specific: multiple independent reports describe withdrawals marked as completed in the Octa dashboard while funds never reached the trader's bank. This is not a processing delay — it is a discrepancy between what the system shows and what actually happens. Reports from publicly available sources name this pattern particularly for larger withdrawals and bank transfer payouts.

If your withdrawal stalls, here is the escalation path that works: first, screenshot the completed status in your dashboard. Second, contact support via live chat and request a transaction reference number. Third, take that reference to your bank and file a trace request. If the broker cannot provide a valid transaction reference for a withdrawal marked completed, you have grounds to escalate via your payment provider's chargeback mechanism (for card deposits) or file a complaint with the relevant regulator. For CySEC-entity clients, the Financial Ombudsman of Cyprus is your route. For offshore-entity clients — you have no external dispute resolution body with enforcement power.

NAFT has not independently tested Octa withdrawals. Submit your withdrawal proof at naft.com/withdrawal-proofs to help other traders.

sections.body: This broker has a narrow profile of trader it genuinely suits — and a much wider profile of trader it could actively harm. The product-market fit only works if you go in with eyes open about what you are getting and what you are giving up.

sections.heading: How to Open an Octa Account — Step by Step
sections.body: The onboarding process is fast and minimal compared to most brokers — which cuts both ways. Low friction to get in also means lower KYC barriers, which is part of why regulators in multiple countries have flagged the platform.

steps.title: Register
steps.detail: Visit the Octa website and sign up with your email or phone number. Account creation takes under 2 minutes. You will be assigned to an entity based on your country of residence — check which entity appears in your client agreement immediately.

steps.title: Verify your identity (KYC)
steps.detail: Upload a government-issued ID (passport or national ID) and proof of address. Octa states verification is typically completed within 24 hours. Some users report same-day approval.

steps.title: Fund your account and test a withdrawal
steps.detail: Deposit the $25 minimum. Place one trade. Then immediately request a withdrawal of any amount. Time it. If the money reaches your bank or e-wallet within 24 hours, you know the pipeline works for your specific method and region. Only then consider scaling your deposit.

sections.practical_note: Make a small deposit. Place one trade. Request a withdrawal immediately. If it processes cleanly, scale with confidence. If it does not — you have lost $25, not $5,000.

sections.heading: Octa Final Verdict — Is It Worth It in 2026?
sections.body:
NAFT scores Octa 5.2 out of 10 — below average, dragged down by a legitimate regulatory crisis that no amount of competitive spreads can offset. The CySEC licence is real (372/18). The zero-commission structure genuinely saves you money versus most ECN-style brokers. And the OctaTrader platform is one of the better beginner tools on the market. But none of that matters if the organisation behind the product cannot guarantee the safety of your funds while its founder faces criminal prosecution.

The risks are not hypothetical. An Rs 800 crore money laundering chargesheet has been filed. $271 million in crypto has been frozen. CySEC has forcibly restructured governance. Multiple regulators across Asia and Europe have issued warnings. And 2026 withdrawal reports document the worst pattern possible — completed statuses with no money arriving. These are not allegations from anonymous forums. They are public enforcement actions from named government agencies.

If you still want to use Octa, keep your balance under $500, withdraw profits the same week you earn them, and have a second broker fully verified and funded as your primary account. NAFT recommends Exness or Pepperstone for traders who want competitive spreads without the counterparty anxiety. Check our full broker comparison for alternatives that match your region.

faq.q: Is Octa a legit broker or a scam?
faq.a: Octa holds a legitimate CySEC licence (372/18) in Cyprus, which makes it a regulated broker within the EU. But the distinction matters: most global clients are not on the CySEC entity. They are on an offshore MISA-licensed entity in Saint Lucia with no investor compensation. The CySEC entity itself has had its majority shareholder barred from management following a fraud probe. Octa is legit on paper — but the organisational risk is elevated in 2026.

faq.q: How long does Octa withdrawal take?
faq.a: Octa states most withdrawals process within 24 hours, with e-wallet payouts often completing in under 19 minutes. Independent reports confirm e-wallet withdrawals (Skrill, Neteller) generally process same-day. Bank transfers take 1-5 business days. Documented 2026 complaints exist where Octa marked withdrawals as completed while funds did not reach the destination — particularly on larger bank transfer payouts.

faq.q: Is Octa regulated by the FCA?
faq.a: No. Octa does not hold an FCA licence. The FCA has issued warnings against clone entities using the OctaFX name (specifically Octafxtrade/octainvestment.net). The legitimate Octa entity in Europe operates under CySEC in Cyprus, not the FCA in the UK. UK residents should verify they are accessing the correct domain and understand that no FCA protection applies to any Octa entity.

faq.q: What is the Octa minimum deposit in 2026?
faq.a: Octa's minimum deposit is $25 across all account types — OctaTrader, MT4, and MT5. This applies to card and e-wallet deposits. Bank transfers have a higher minimum of approximately $100. The $25 entry point makes Octa accessible for micro-budget testing, though NAFT recommends depositing only what you can afford to lose given the broker's current regulatory situation.

faq.q: What happened with Octa and Elev8 in 2026?
faq.a: In February 2026, the Mauritius and Comoros-based entities that previously operated under the Octa brand separated and relaunched as Elev8. The split was described as a termination of a brand-sharing agreement. The CySEC-regulated Cyprus entity and the FSCA South Africa entity did not join Elev8 and continue operating under the Octa name. If you were previously an Octa client under the Mauritius or Comoros entities, you are now an Elev8 client.

faq.q: Is Octa safe for traders in South Africa?
faq.a: Octa holds an FSCA licence in South Africa, which means it operates under local derivative trading regulations and is required to segregate client funds. There is no compensation scheme under the FSCA — your protection is limited to fund segregation. South African traders are arguably better positioned than offshore-entity clients, but should still monitor the broader corporate governance situation given the India enforcement probe against the brand's founder.

faq.q: Does Octa charge commission on trades?
faq.a: No. Octa charges zero commission on all account types. Your only trading cost is the spread — averaging 0.6 pips on EUR/USD for OctaTrader and MT5 accounts, and 0.9 pips on MT4. This translates to an all-in cost of $6.00-$9.00 per standard lot round-turn depending on your platform. No inactivity fees, no deposit fees, and no withdrawal fees are charged by Octa.

Leverage depends entirely on which entity holds your account. CySEC entity (EU/EEA residents): 1:30 on majors, 1:20 on minors, 1:10 on commodities — standard EU retail caps. Offshore MISA entity (most global clients): up to 1:500. The headline 1:500 leverage only applies to the offshore entity with zero investor protection. High leverage without a safety net is not a feature — it is how undercapitalised accounts get wiped in seconds.
